# Roger Clevenger — Principal Site Reliability Engineer

Canonical portfolio: https://rclevenger-hm.github.io/portfolio/
GitHub: https://github.com/rclevenger-hm
Machine-readable JSON: https://rclevenger-hm.github.io/portfolio/data/profile.json

## Professional focus
Principal-level site reliability and DevOps engineering focused on cloud infrastructure, reliability engineering, observability, incident response, infrastructure as code, CI/CD, distributed systems, and operational automation.

## Engineering principles
- Make failure legible.
- Bound the cost of being wrong.
- Design recovery with the system.
- Design for ownership transfer.
- Distinguish implemented behavior from planned work and production-readiness claims.

## Core capabilities
Cloud and infrastructure: AWS, Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, Terraform, networking, compute, storage, identity.
Reliability engineering: SLO thinking, incident response, failure analysis, recovery, capacity planning, runbooks.
Delivery and automation: GitHub Actions, Jenkins, Docker, Packer, Ansible, Python, release engineering.
Observability: Datadog, Grafana, CloudWatch, metrics, logs, alerting, operational dashboards.
Distributed and data systems: Kafka, Hadoop, Databricks, Snowflake, OpenSearch.
Engineering systems: JavaScript, TypeScript, APIs, serverless systems, browser applications, operational tooling.

## Public engineering evidence

### Sports Gamecast
Repository: https://github.com/rclevenger-hm/sports-gamecast
Signals: browser reliability, CI/CD, defensive parsing, state-aware refresh, favorites, notifications, broadcast mapping.
Decision: keep the application static and dependency-light while using defensive runtime behavior and deterministic browser tests to control uncertainty in upstream sports data.
Boundary: the current sports data dependency is undocumented and is not represented as a supported production contract.

### OCI Ephemeral Resource Janitor
Repository: https://github.com/rclevenger-hm/oci-ephemeral-resource-janitor
Case study: https://rclevenger-hm.github.io/portfolio/case-studies/oci-ephemeral-resource-janitor/
Signals: explicit opt-in lifecycle ownership, dry-run defaults, protected-resource policy, fail-closed TTL/expiration parsing, per-run action caps, separate termination interlock, two-phase stop-then-terminate behavior, structured audit reporting.
Decision: require explicit lifecycle ownership and layer reversible defaults, bounded actions, protection policy, validation, and independent termination permission before destructive OCI lifecycle actions are permitted.
Boundary: this enforces policy for explicitly ephemeral resources; it does not infer idle resources from utilization and currently supports OCI Compute instances.

### Identity Document Async Pipeline
Repository: https://github.com/rclevenger-hm/driver_license_authenticity_lambda
Signals: AWS Lambda, S3, SQS, dead-letter queue, DynamoDB, API Gateway, Terraform.
Decision: separate request acceptance from background screening and persist job state so asynchronous work, retries, and failure recovery are explicit operating concerns.
Boundary: the project performs plausibility screening and is not legal proof of document authenticity.

### Kafka on OCI
Repository: https://github.com/rclevenger-hm/kafka-oci-deployment
Signals: KRaft, private networking, capacity, quorum, observability, recovery planning.
Decision: treat consensus, network topology, storage, recovery headroom, and operational signals as one distributed-systems reliability envelope.
Boundary: executable provisioning and automated failure validation remain follow-up work.
